quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic is moving in one direction only.
Traffic is moving in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to keep to the right side of the divider ahead.

questions.question: What should you do if your tire blows out?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not use your brakes right away.
Slowly reduce speed and pull to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, take your foot off the gas and do not brake immediately. Gradually slow down, then gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: Stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: What time of day it is.
What condition your tires are in.

questions.correctAnswerText: What time of day it is.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, road conditions, brake quality, tire condition, and speed. The time of day does not affect how far it takes to stop.

questions.question: If you are driving very slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right and let other cars pass.
Do not let the other cars pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and let other cars pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is unsafe. If traffic backs up behind you on a two-lane road, you must pull over and let the other vehicles pass.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?
questions.correctAnswerText: A warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to hazards or special situations ahead.

questions.question: How much road space are motorcycles entitled to?

options.text: The full width of a lane, like other vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The full width of a lane, like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use the entire lane width, just like all other vehicles.

questions.question: A car is coming toward you on the left, and a bicycle is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Let the car pass first, then pass the bicycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first, then pass the bicycle.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass, then safely pass the bicycle. Do not try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: Another driver wants to pass your car. What should you do?

options.text: Signal the other driver when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming cars and slow down to let them pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming cars and slow down to let them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right when someone passes you. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to help the other vehicle merge back into your lane safely.

questions.question: When is it important to slow down?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, on sharp or blind curves, where there are pedestrians or hazards, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only to the left and right of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: All around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep a space cushion on all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn your steering wheel?

options.text: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle skids, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want it to go. Once the vehicle starts to straighten out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: When can a driver legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: If the vehicle is turning left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if it means driving off the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the vehicle is turning left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right of a vehicle turning left if a passing lane is available. You may also pass on the right on a road with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What is true about blind spots on larger vehicles?

options.text: They are the same size as on smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are larger.
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have larger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near their rear that cannot be seen in their side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: The possible speeds for the area.
The highest or lowest speed you are legally allowed to drive.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in poor conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed you are legally allowed to drive.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest safe speed allowed on a road. The maximum speed is for ideal conditions. You must slow down when conditions require it.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard ahead. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection, the traffic light turns from green to yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross before the red light.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will soon turn red. Be prepared to stop for the red light if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Signs that tell drivers about hazardous conditions are called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to potential dangers ahead. Follow warning signs for your safety. Ignoring a warning sign can lead to accidents.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. Stop at the stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: If your turn signals do not work, what should you use to show you are turning?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals.
questions.explanation: When your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to show when you are turning.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: The same thing as a stop sign.
You do not have to stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.
